I wrote this wiki entry to onboard technical writers to the project. Beyond explaining our current workflow, it covers key technical concepts so writers can build autonomy and apply what they learn across other projects.

---

# Extension Kit and App Studio

Unit4 Extension Kit is a toolkit for extending Unit4 applications. It lets customers author and deploy new capabilities as microservices, connect them into flows. App Studio, included within Extension Kit, turns those flows into custom apps that let end users interact with the new capabilities.

Since App Studio is part of Extension Kit, its documentation lives within Extension Kit's documentation too.

We publish the documentation in two sites:

- [Knowledge Hub](#), meant for internal use and restricted to Unit4 users. It contains all the files published on the external site, plus some additional internal-only files.
- An [external site](https://docs-external.u4pp.com/extensions-kit/), meant for the end users. Its typical reader is a _citizen developer_ – someone with some technical background who still expects technical concepts to be explained in approachable, non-expert terms.

You can find the App Studio section under **My Apps** in the navigation bar.

> [!TIP]
> The external site is indexed by all main search engines. This means you can [use AI to find information quicker](https://docs-external.u4pp.com/extensions-kit/using-ai-for-documentation/).

## Documentation organisation

The documentation for both products lives inside a single repository: [U4.ExtensionsKit.Documentation](#). This repository only stores the documentation itself and the necessary files to build the site.

The documentation is written in Markdown files (.md) and is organised across the folder `docs/` and its subfolders. The documentation specific to App Studio is in `docs/app-studio/`.

## MkDocs

Both sites are generated using [MkDocs](https://www.mkdocs.org/). MkDocs is a static site generator that converts the .md files into .html files and links them together. To structure the information and decide what files to include in the site, we use the file `mkdocs.yml`.

This file controls what pages are included in the site, how they relate to each other, and how they will look:

```yml
# U4.ExtensionsKit.Documentation/mkdocs.yml

site_name: Extension Kit
extra_css: [css/extra.css]
theme_dir: unit4_theme
extra:
  pplink: https://thehub.unit4.com/
pages:
  - Introduction:
      - "Welcome": "index.md"
      - "Release notes": "release-notes.md"
      - "AI guidelines": "using-ai-for-documentation.md"
  - How to use:
      - Extension Kit Portal:
          - "Overview": "guides/portal/overview.md"
          - "How to access the portal": "guides/portal/access.md"
          - "Monitoring": "guides/portal/monitoring.md"
          - "My Flows":
              - "Flow overview": "guides/portal/flow-overview.md"
              - "Create a flow": "guides/portal/create-a-flow.md"
              - "Run a flow manually": "guides/portal/run-flow.md"
          - "My Apps - App Studio":
              - "About App Studio": "app-studio/about-app-studio-internal.md"
              - "Release notes": "app-studio/release-notes-internal.md"
              - "Getting started":
                  - "Dashboard": "app-studio/get-started/dashboard.md"
                  - "Create or import an app": "app-studio/get-started/how-to-create-app.md"
```

Your main focus as a Documentation Developer is to maintain the `pages` section. This section shapes layout in the navigation, and is built from two kinds of entries:

- A **group**, such as `How to use` or `My Flows`, which nests further entries underneath it to create a collapsible section in the navigation.
- A **page**, written as `"Title": "path/to/file.md"`, which links directly to a file.

The files included will be available to the user, while all others will be excluded from the final build.

On Knowledge Hub, a file excluded from `pages` is still built and reachable directly by URL (which mirrors the file's path in `docs/`), it just will not appear in the navigation bar.

> [!TIP]
> Indentation matters in .yml files to establish the hierarchy of the files. For more information, see the [official YAML documentation](https://www.yaml.info/learn/index.html).

Since we publish two versions of the documentation, there are two `mkdocs.yml` files with a different structure. The version for Knowledge Hub is in the root of the repository and the version for the external site is inside the folder `external/`.

## Set up your local environment

### Install Python

MkDocs is powered by Python. You need to install Python to be able to install and run MkDocs. The easiest way to install it is through the [Microsoft Store](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9nq7512cxl7t). Once installed, you will be able to execute Python commands on your command-line interface (CLI) of choice. Run the following command to see your current Python version:

```shell
py --version
```

### Set up a virtual environment

Even though you now have the latest Python version installed, the Extension Kit repository uses older Python and MkDocs versions. You could downgrade and adapt to match the requirements for this project, but if you manage other MkDocs projects you will run into compatibility issues. The best approach is to create **virtual environments**, this will allow each project to keep their own dependencies isolated without affecting the others.

To set up a virtual environment, navigate to the repository directory in your CLI of choice. In the case of Extension Kit, you will need Python version 3.7.9.

Run the following commands to install that Python version and create a folder named `venv` that will contain all the necessary files to run Python inside the virtual environment:

```shell
py install 3.7.9
py -3.7 -m venv venv
```

To activate the virtual environment, run:

```shell
venv\Scripts\activate
```

You are now running a Python 3.7.9 session. This continues until you close your current CLI instance, or until you run the following command:

```shell
deactivate
```

### Install MkDocs in the virtual environment

While your virtual environment session is active, execute the following command to install MkDocs and the necessary dependency:

```shell
pip install mkdocs==0.17.5 markdown==3.3.7
```

Now you have access to the `mkdocs` command as long as you are in the virtual environment session:

```shell
mkdocs --version
mkdocs --help
```

### Run the site locally

To publish the site locally and view it in your browser, run:

```shell
mkdocs serve
```

This will build the Knowledge Hub version of the documentation and make it available in this URL that only you can see: http://127.0.0.1:8000.

To stop the server, press `Ctrl`+`C` on the CLI or just close the CLI window.

To build the external site instead, you will first have to navigate to the `external/` directory before executing the MkDocs command:

```shell
cd external/
mkdocs serve
```

## Git workflow

### Branches

There are two permanent branches: **main** and **EXTERNAL**. Knowledge Hub is built from **main**, which is always up to date. The external site is built from **EXTERNAL**, which only receives commits once they are ready to release externally.

### Git cycle

1. Create your branch off **main** using the pattern `doc/<task-number>-<descriptive-text>`, for example `doc/876678-quick-tip`.
2. Create, edit, or delete the relevant files.
3. If you added, moved, or removed a page, update the `mkdocs.yml` files so it is reflected in the navigation.
4. Commit your changes and create a PR.

### Pull requests

Following the migration to GitHub, pull requests in this repository do not yet have a policy to automatically add the relevant teams as required reviewers. Until this policy is implemented, manually add as reviewers the people involved in the feature you are documenting and at least one other Documentation Developer.

Do not set your PR to autocomplete. Merging to **main** publishes immediately to Knowledge Hub, so you must complete the merge manually once you have confirmed it is the right time to publish.

## Release process

### How and when to release

- **During regular development:** merge your PRs to **main**. This publishes to Knowledge Hub immediately, whether or not the underlying functionality has been released yet.
- **If a change should not go external yet:** keep track of which commits are still waiting to go external and what they depend on.
- **On release day:** once the feature is live on non-production environments, publish every commit that is now ready to the external site and follow the steps in [Publish to the external site](#publish-to-the-external-site).
- **Hotfixes:** use the same process as release day.

### Publish to the external site

#### Cherry-pick

**EXTERNAL** only ever grows through cherry-picks from **main**. This gives you full control over what reaches external, while keeping its commit history in the same order as **main**.

1. For each commit ready to go external, cherry-pick it onto **EXTERNAL**:

   ```shell
   git cherry-pick <commit-id>
   ```

2. Push the branch.
3. [Run the external pipeline](#run-the-external-pipeline).

#### Run the external pipeline

This pipeline can publish to both Knowledge Hub and the external site. Publishing to Knowledge Hub happens automatically, while publishing to the external site requires you to manually run and approve this pipeline.

1. Go to **Azure DevOps** > **People Platform and Fundamentals** > **Pipelines** > **All** > **Extension Kit** > **EK - Documentation**.
2. Click **Run pipeline**.
3. Select the **EXTERNAL** branch from the drop-down list.

> [!WARNING]
> Make sure **EXTERNAL** already contains the documentation you want to release before running the pipeline. See [Cherry-pick](#cherry-pick).

4. Under **Stages to run**, select only the last stage, **PP External Docs publication**. If you skip this, the branch will also publish to Knowledge Hub.

   ![Stages to run](data:image/png;base64,)

> [!TIP]
> If you select the wrong stages by mistake, simply rerun the pipeline and do not approve the external stage.

1. Click **Run**.

   ![Run pipeline](data:image/png;base64,)

2. Once ready, approve the last stage by clicking **Review** to release to external.

   ![Pipeline run approval](data:image/png;base64,)

Once the pipeline run finishes, the changes will be live on the external site.
